main_text.p: mūm ebulliens ex pultario in ignem effundi, famina aut ancilla statim omne opus relin- quat, accurratque ut pultarium ab igne re- moveat; (id quidem familiare mulierculis ubivis esse crediderim, ne {c}ilicet lactis damnum patiantur;) sed addit, mox tempore eodem manipulo Salis pri- mam, in quam lac effundebatur, confper- gere: si vero curid faciant ex illis perconterin; dicere, fieri hoc ad prohibendum, ne vacca ex qua lac effufum emulgebatur antea, ex uberum dolore laboret: nisi enim hac agerent, tur, illa duritiem contrahere & exulcerari, imo etiam vaccam sanguinem mingere, peri- culumque esse, ne ex hoc malo moriatur, &c. Oporteret utique illas mulierculas Anglicanas Philosophiae valde gnaras exiftere, quae tam prompte valent morborum caufas indagare, atque re- media illis curandis idonea ex naturae abstrusioribus recessibus eruere! vel mirum profecto, quis illud mulierculis circa vaccas occupatis, primus suggesse- rit? page.notes: Words in the text are partly illegible in the scan and read as best possible; the line "mūm ebulliens" and "{c}ilicet" are doubtful; "ebulliens" [?] and several words in lines 1-4 are uncertain. Page number 592 is read from the printed "59 2" at top left. Catchword "mor-" at foot right is a hyphenated word-break and is given as the last line of text.
